_why: One synthetic catalog and one set of render vectors, shared by the server-pure, client-pure, DOM and mutant tests so the two independent implementations of the render rule cannot drift. Pure ASCII and visibly synthetic: the product catalog ships EMPTY until the evaluating radiologist supplies the first exam and its fields (P6/D2), and nothing in here may ever be reachable from product code or HTTP (P7).

invalid.why: not one of the catalog choices
more decimals than the catalog fixes
a string is not a number
a string is not a boolean

_productCatalogSha256_why: sha256 of the canonical JSON (sorted keys, separators ',' and ':') of the PRODUCT catalog. T1 asserts it for the compiled STRUCTURE_CATALOG, T2 for PRODUCT_CATALOG - the two constants are compared as VALUES, neither reads the other's source, and neither test can see the other's file. It changes the day a real catalog ships, and that is the point: the change has to be made here, deliberately, in the same commit.

catalogVectors.name: accept: the shipped synthetic catalog
catalogVectors.why: the SYN-T1 fixture every other suite already uses must stay legal

catalogVectors.name: accept: empty
catalogVectors.why: the product default; normal operation, no diagnostic, no console output

catalogVectors.name: accept: distinct prefixes
catalogVectors.why: R-B separates on the opening literal

catalogVectors.name: accept: same prefix, distinct suffixes
catalogVectors.why: R-B separates on the closing literal: a line ending in ' mm' is never one ending in ' cm'

catalogVectors.name: accept: same frame, disjoint vocabularies
catalogVectors.why: R-A: both value spaces are finite and fully listed, so the sets are compared exhaustively

catalogVectors.name: accept: empty prefix separated by a distinct suffix
catalogVectors.why: an empty prefix is a prefix of everything, so this pair may only separate by suffix - and it does

catalogVectors.name: accept: different fields never meet
catalogVectors.why: presence is counted per field, so the same sentence in two fields is not a collision

catalogVectors.name: accept: cross-template, distinct prefixes
catalogVectors.why: the pairwise check reaches across templates, and separated items stay legal there too

catalogVectors.name: accept: ordinary precomposed Hangul literals
catalogVectors.why: R-S refuses composition ACROSS the boundary, not Hangul; precomposed syllables are ordinary text

catalogVectors.name: accept: R-S stable partner of the Hangul witness
catalogVectors.why: the same shape as the first R-S witness, but a space stands between the two jamo

catalogVectors.name: R-S: Hangul L+V across the prefix boundary
catalogVectors.why: U+1100 + U+1161 compose to U+AC00 under NFC; BOTH have canonical combining class 0, so a ccc rule misses it

catalogVectors.name: R-S: Hangul LV+T across the prefix boundary
catalogVectors.why: U+AC00 + U+11A8 compose to U+AC01; ccc 0 again

catalogVectors.name: R-S: across the suffix boundary
catalogVectors.why: the composition happens at the closing boundary instead

catalogVectors.name: R-S: Indic vowel sign across the prefix boundary
catalogVectors.why: U+09C7 + U+09BE compose to U+09CB; a third script, same ccc-0 shape - the rule is not Hangul-specific

catalogVectors.name: R-S: a non-zero ccc mark carried by a choice text
catalogVectors.why: the combining ring composes with the literal A; one rule covers both families

catalogVectors.name: R-C: two choice texts render one line
catalogVectors.why: the stored code could not be recovered from the sentence

catalogVectors.name: R-C: two choice texts that differ only in normalisation
catalogVectors.why: the presence equation NFCs the line, so these two ARE one line - byte inequality proves nothing

catalogVectors.name: R-C: boolean words are equal
catalogVectors.why: true and false would be indistinguishable in the record

catalogVectors.name: R-A: same frame, overlapping vocabularies
catalogVectors.why: the exhaustive comparison finds the shared line

catalogVectors.name: R-B: same skeleton, choice vs free text
catalogVectors.why: before this unit these landed in two buckets that never met, so both passed

catalogVectors.name: R-B: distinct skeletons that still collide
catalogVectors.why: values 'x tail' and 'A: x' both render 'A: x tail': skeleton uniqueness was never sufficient

catalogVectors.name: R-B: cross-template, same field
catalogVectors.why: collisions cross template boundaries; the shipped rule only looked within one template

catalogVectors.name: R-B: one suffix is a suffix of the other
catalogVectors.why: 'Size: 5 mm' is reachable from both

catalogVectors.name: R-B: empty prefix with an empty-suffix partner
catalogVectors.why: empty literals are prefixes and suffixes of everything, so neither side separates

catalogVectors.name: R-D: NFD literal
catalogVectors.why: R-B compares the literals as written, so they must already be NFC

catalogVectors.why: the shipped validator accepted this before this unit; the line would reach jsonb as a 500

catalogVectors.name: R-D: lone surrogate in a choice text
catalogVectors.why: the same hole reached through the choice vocabulary

catalogVectors.name: R-D: no slot
catalogVectors.why: nowhere to put the value

catalogVectors.why: P10: one entry is one line, or the citation guards would have to grow a structured union

catalogVectors.why: no value could ever fit

catalogVectors.why: a blank line cannot be found in a report body, so its presence could never be judged

catalogVectors.name: R-D: an enumerable value renders past the byte limit
catalogVectors.why: the literals fit on their own, but this value can never be stored

catalogVectors.name: R-D: revision below 1
catalogVectors.why: revisions start at 1

catalogVectors.name: R-D: duplicate templateId
catalogVectors.why: two templates answering to one id: the second would shadow the first in every lookup

catalogVectors.name: R-D: duplicate item code in one template
catalogVectors.why: without this check the pair is legal (R-B separates them) and a stored itemCode names two items

catalogVectors.name: R-D: duplicate choice code
catalogVectors.why: a stored value could not be resolved to one choice; deleting the check turns this into R-C, not ACCEPT

catalogVectors.name: R-D: a field that is not a report field
catalogVectors.why: presence is counted per field, so an unknown field has nowhere to be counted

catalogVectors.why: the stored entry would fail isStructureEntry and make the whole read unknown

catalogVectors.name: R-D: missing label
catalogVectors.why: the screen has nothing to name the control with

catalogVectors.name: R-D: a null template element
catalogVectors.why: the server answers R-D through template?.templateId; the browser must not raise an untyped TypeError here, because create() rethrows it and that kills the whole page script

catalogVectors.name: R-D: a null item element
catalogVectors.why: same shape one level down (item?.code)

catalogVectors.name: R-D: a null choice element
catalogVectors.why: same shape two levels down (choice?.code)

catalogVectors.name: R-D: number min/max are null
catalogVectors.why: a coercing isFinite() says null is finite; Number.isFinite does not

catalogVectors.name: R-D: number min/max are numeric strings
catalogVectors.why: the same coercion hole, reached through a string

catalogVectors.name: R-D: number min/max are booleans
catalogVectors.why: Number.isFinite(true) is false; a Python oracle using isinstance(x, int) would accept it, because bool is a subclass of int

catalogVectors.name: shape: the catalog itself is not an array
catalogVectors.why: `x ?? []` only turns null/undefined into an empty list. An object walked by for..of raised an untyped TypeError on the server and was silently skipped by the browser's index loop, so a malformed catalog looked legal on one side and killed the page script on the other.

catalogVectors.name: shape: items is not an array
catalogVectors.why: items: {} skipped the browser loop and left a LIVE form holding a template with no reachable item, while the server raised a TypeError with no rule name.

catalogVectors.name: shape: choices is an array-like object, not an array
catalogVectors.why: {length: 1, "0": {...}} is the shape that split the two implementations: for..of raised on the server, the browser's index loop walked it and accepted. Neither answer is a rule.

catalogVectors.name: accept: the same template with an empty items array
catalogVectors.why: the partner of the items case: an ARRAY with nothing in it is legal, so the refusal above is about the container and not about emptiness.

catalogVectors.name: accept: the same choice item with a real array
catalogVectors.why: the partner of the choices case: identical item, identical single choice, carried in a real array.

catalogVectors.name: shape: choices is a bare number
catalogVectors.why: the partner shape that separates the THIRD rule from the other two: the browser and the server both reach R-D through `.length` being undefined, but the Python oracle without an isinstance check walks straight into a TypeError - an oracle that crashes cannot judge, and a judge that cannot judge is not a third opinion.

_catalogVectors_why: One catalog per case with the rule it must trip; ACCEPT means the whole catalog is legal. Check order is R-D, R-S, R-C, then pairs R-A before R-B, so a case names the FIRST rule it violates. Every rejection case has an accepted partner of the same shape, so a validator that simply refused everything would fail here. The Unicode cases carry literal code points (U+1100, U+1161, U+AC00, U+11A8, U+09C7, U+09BE, U+030A, U+00C5 and lone surrogates) rather than escapes, so every consumer sees the same string without re-decoding. The shape cases (null template, null item, null choice) and the bounds cases exist because a malformed catalog must be refused with a RULE on both sides: an untyped throw in the browser escapes create() and takes the whole page script down with it. A JSON file cannot express a sparse array hole, so that witness is built in the JS tests instead. The container-shape cases (catalog, items and choices that are not arrays, including an array-LIKE object) each carry an accepted partner of the same shape, so they pin the container and not emptiness. Synthetic only: no clinical item, label, unit, range, vocabulary or sentence is authored here.

entryVectors.name: R-S entry: Hangul L+V at the prefix boundary
entryVectors.why: a free-text value is not in the catalog, so the catalog check cannot see it - only the entry check can

entryVectors.name: accept entry: the same item with a value that does not compose
entryVectors.why: the partner: the same item and the same boundary, refused only because of the value

entryVectors.name: R-S entry: Hangul LV+T at the prefix boundary
accept entry: LV prefix with an ordinary value
R-S entry: at the suffix boundary
entryVectors.why: the value's last character composes with the first character of the closing literal

entryVectors.name: accept entry: the same suffix with an ordinary value
R-S entry: a combining ring after a literal A
entryVectors.why: U+030A has a non-zero combining class; this is the family a ccc rule would have caught, kept as a case

entryVectors.name: accept entry: the same item with a value that starts with a letter
R-S entry: an Indic vowel sign at the prefix boundary
accept entry: the same Indic prefix with an ordinary value
accept entry: a decomposed Hangul value after '= '
entryVectors.why: the value composes WITHIN itself, which the presence equation already normalises; nothing crosses the boundary, so it is accepted and stored exactly as typed - R-E would have refused this

entryVectors.name: accept entry: a value ending in a combining mark before ' u'
entryVectors.why: the closing literal starts with a space, so the mark has nothing to compose with - R-E refused every such value for no safety gain

_entryVectors_why: Free text and numbers are not in the catalog, so the load-time check cannot see their values; the entry check is where R-S reaches them. Each catalog here is a single legal item, so the only thing a case can trip is the entry rule. The server drives these through structureApplyInput (after its byte-equality check), the browser through validateValue. The last two are the over-restriction cases: they must be ACCEPTED, and they are exactly the values a combining-class rule would have refused.
